The [two-collision and original-cutoff audit](../fzz-p-screening-collision-continuation.md) proves the exact convergence boundaries, both local finite parts and the forced coefficient. The [whole-space cutoff audit](../fzz-p-plane-screening-cutoff-matching.md) retains both local terms and the exterior and proves convergence for independently removed punctures. Must still justify equality with any proposed continued family before transferring its parameter responses.

# CCM-FU: recovering a prepared terminal budget

- Stage: 1-in-progress.
- Target: a bounded complete path through an actual terminal core under a small quadratic envelope.
- Full chain: divisor source → renewable signed reserve → exhaustive prime selection → uniform signed Abel bound → RH.

For a fixed quotient bound J, a sufficiently large cutoff makes every
remaining prime terminal. Its singleton has absolute value at most
(3/5) J sqrt(M). Thus the remaining square energy is at most
(9/25) J² M times the number of primes below M, uniformly in the processed
core. Prime sparsity makes this o(M²).

The producer processes every prime outside a positive quotient-seven
window and a negative late window. Existing quantitative PNT bounds give
the final signed aggregate little-o of M sqrt(M)/log(M), while each
reserved window has a positive lower mass on that scale. The exact
terminal sum identity therefore places the new head within the interval
that the two opposite supplies can cancel. A finite mass cover reduces
the head to within one source weight, with no assumed initial energy
bound. The remaining square energy and complete successor envelope then
fit any fixed positive quadratic budget at sufficiently large cutoff.

The [unconditional endpoint construction](../3-formalized/ccm-fu-small-terminal-core.md)
is formalized: every prime outside the two windows is processed, all
square-root-scale primes are processed, the head is at most 5 sqrt(M),
and the complete successor envelope is at most ε M² for any fixed ε>0
eventually. The new density estimate, discrete head cover, actual source
transfer, and mass comparison close that endpoint construction.

The construction supplies a prepared endpoint. It does not supply a
uniformly bounded path from the initial state to that endpoint, renew
exhausted sources, or bound the final signed Abel sum. Existing terminal
ordering retains that final sum as an endpoint obligation.

import GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower.RiemannGaussian.RiemannXiBlaschkeLogDerivativeSummability

/-!
# Complete signed variation and phase dispersion

Absolute summability of the selected signed Blaschke logarithmic-derivative
terms gives finite complete limits for their `l1` variation, cancellation,
and pairwise phase dispersion.  The finite-window dispersion identity passes
to these limits.

The resulting static invariants give a sharp rigidity formulation: at every
noncolliding upper observation point, RH is equivalent to simultaneous
vanishing of the complete signed resultant and complete phase dispersion.
-/

open Complex Filter MeasureTheory Metric Polynomial Set Topology
open scoped Classical ENNReal Interval Topology

namespace RiemannGaussian

noncomputable section

/-- Complete `l1` variation of the absolutely summable signed upper Blaschke
logarithmic-derivative terms. -/
def riemannXiUpperBlaschkeCompleteLogDerivativeVariation (z : ℂ) : ℝ :=
  ∑' rho : NontrivialZetaZero,
    ‖zetaUpperBlaschkeSelectedLogDerivativeSummand z rho‖

/-- Complete triangle-cancellation gap of the signed upper Blaschke series. -/
def riemannXiUpperBlaschkeCompleteLogDerivativeCancellation (z : ℂ) : ℝ :=
  riemannXiUpperBlaschkeCompleteLogDerivativeVariation z -
    ‖riemannXiUpperBlaschkeCompleteLogDerivative z‖

/-- Complete pairwise phase dispersion of the signed upper Blaschke series. -/
def riemannXiUpperBlaschkeCompletePhaseDispersion (z : ℂ) : ℝ :=
  riemannXiUpperBlaschkeCompleteLogDerivativeVariation z ^ 2 -
    ‖riemannXiUpperBlaschkeCompleteLogDerivative z‖ ^ 2

/-- The complete resultant norm is bounded by complete termwise variation. -/
theorem norm_riemannXiUpperBlaschkeCompleteLogDerivative_le_variation
    {z : ℂ} (hz : 0 < z.im) (hxi : riemannXiSpectral z ≠ 0) :
    ‖riemannXiUpperBlaschkeCompleteLogDerivative z‖ ≤
      riemannXiUpperBlaschkeCompleteLogDerivativeVariation z := by
  unfold riemannXiUpperBlaschkeCompleteLogDerivative
    riemannXiUpperBlaschkeCompleteLogDerivativeVariation
  exact norm_tsum_le_tsum_norm
    (summable_zetaUpperBlaschkeSelectedLogDerivativeSummand hz hxi).norm

/-- Complete signed-series cancellation is nonnegative. -/
theorem riemannXiUpperBlaschkeCompleteLogDerivativeCancellation_nonneg
    {z : ℂ} (hz : 0 < z.im) (hxi : riemannXiSpectral z ≠ 0) :
    0 ≤ riemannXiUpperBlaschkeCompleteLogDerivativeCancellation z := by
  unfold riemannXiUpperBlaschkeCompleteLogDerivativeCancellation
  exact sub_nonneg.mpr
    (norm_riemannXiUpperBlaschkeCompleteLogDerivative_le_variation hz hxi)

/-- Complete phase dispersion is nonnegative. -/
theorem riemannXiUpperBlaschkeCompletePhaseDispersion_nonneg
    {z : ℂ} (hz : 0 < z.im) (hxi : riemannXiSpectral z ≠ 0) :
    0 ≤ riemannXiUpperBlaschkeCompletePhaseDispersion z := by
  have hnorm :=
    norm_riemannXiUpperBlaschkeCompleteLogDerivative_le_variation hz hxi
  have hnorm0 : 0 ≤ ‖riemannXiUpperBlaschkeCompleteLogDerivative z‖ :=
    norm_nonneg _
  unfold riemannXiUpperBlaschkeCompletePhaseDispersion
  nlinarith

/-- Exact complete factorization of phase dispersion into cancellation times
the sum of variation and resultant norm. -/
theorem riemannXiUpperBlaschkeCompletePhaseDispersion_eq_cancellation_mul_add
    (z : ℂ) :
    riemannXiUpperBlaschkeCompletePhaseDispersion z =
      riemannXiUpperBlaschkeCompleteLogDerivativeCancellation z *
        (riemannXiUpperBlaschkeCompleteLogDerivativeVariation z +
          ‖riemannXiUpperBlaschkeCompleteLogDerivative z‖) := by
  unfold riemannXiUpperBlaschkeCompletePhaseDispersion
    riemannXiUpperBlaschkeCompleteLogDerivativeCancellation
  ring

/-- The square of complete cancellation is bounded by complete phase
dispersion. -/
theorem riemannXiUpperBlaschkeCompleteLogDerivativeCancellation_sq_le_dispersion
    {z : ℂ} (hz : 0 < z.im) (hxi : riemannXiSpectral z ≠ 0) :
    riemannXiUpperBlaschkeCompleteLogDerivativeCancellation z ^ 2 ≤
      riemannXiUpperBlaschkeCompletePhaseDispersion z := by
  have hnorm :=
    norm_riemannXiUpperBlaschkeCompleteLogDerivative_le_variation hz hxi
  have hnorm0 : 0 ≤ ‖riemannXiUpperBlaschkeCompleteLogDerivative z‖ :=
    norm_nonneg _
  unfold riemannXiUpperBlaschkeCompleteLogDerivativeCancellation
    riemannXiUpperBlaschkeCompletePhaseDispersion
  nlinarith

/-- A finite upper window of selected term norms is exactly the existing
finite signed-term variation. -/
theorem sum_norm_zetaUpperBlaschkeSelectedLogDerivativeSummand_eq_variationWindow
    (z : ℂ) (T : ℝ) :
    ∑ rho ∈ spectralZetaZeroWindow T,
        ‖zetaUpperBlaschkeSelectedLogDerivativeSummand z rho‖ =
      riemannXiUpperBlaschkeLogDerivativeVariationWindow z T := by
  unfold zetaUpperBlaschkeSelectedLogDerivativeSummand
    riemannXiUpperBlaschkeLogDerivativeVariationWindow
    spectralUpperZetaZeroWindow
  rw [Finset.sum_filter]
  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
  intro rho _hrho
  by_cases hupper : rho.1.re < 2⁻¹
  · simp [hupper]
  · simp [hupper]

/-!
# Complete-divisor crossed-product smoothness fracture

Functional-equation reflection is smooth for the absolute divisor and genuinely non-Lipschitz for
the signed divisor.  The diagonal Real-corona orientation has the opposite defect: it is smooth
for the signed divisor but commutator-blind.  This is the exact smoothness--detectability tradeoff.
-/

noncomputable section

open Filter HilbertSchmidt
open GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower

namespace RHTower

/-- Linear functional-equation reflection on the complete Xi-divisor Hilbert space. -/
def xiCompleteDivisorReflection : Module.End ℂ XiDivisorL2 where
  toFun := fun a =>
    ⟨fun q => a (xiZeroCopyReflectEquiv q),
      HilbertSchmidt.memℓp_of_sq
        (xiZeroCopyReflectEquiv.summable_iff.mpr
          (HilbertSchmidt.summable_coe_sq a))⟩
  map_add' := by
    intro a b
    ext q
    rfl
  map_smul' := by
    intro c a
    ext q
    rfl

@[simp] theorem xiCompleteDivisorReflection_apply
    (a : XiDivisorL2) (q : XiZeroCopy) :
    xiCompleteDivisorReflection a q = a (xiZeroCopyReflectEquiv q) := rfl

theorem xiCompleteDivisorReflection_sq :
    xiCompleteDivisorReflection * xiCompleteDivisorReflection = 1 := by
  apply LinearMap.ext
  intro a
  ext q
  change a (xiZeroCopyReflectEquiv (xiZeroCopyReflectEquiv q)) = a q
  rw [xiZeroCopyReflectEquiv_apply_apply]

theorem norm_xiCompleteDivisorReflection (a : XiDivisorL2) :
    ‖xiCompleteDivisorReflection a‖ = ‖a‖ := by
  have hsq : ‖xiCompleteDivisorReflection a‖ ^ 2 = ‖a‖ ^ 2 := by
    rw [HilbertSchmidt.lp_norm_sq_eq, HilbertSchmidt.lp_norm_sq_eq]
    exact xiZeroCopyReflectEquiv.tsum_eq (fun q => ‖a q‖ ^ 2)
  nlinarith [norm_nonneg (xiCompleteDivisorReflection a), norm_nonneg a]

/-- Signed complete-divisor energy: canonical orbit orientation times absolute centered energy. -/
def xiCompleteDivisorSignedEnergy (q : XiZeroCopy) : ℝ :=
  (deningerArithmeticFEOrientation q).re * xiCompleteDivisorEnergy q

theorem abs_xiCompleteDivisorSignedEnergy (q : XiZeroCopy) :
    |xiCompleteDivisorSignedEnergy q| = xiCompleteDivisorEnergy q := by
  have heps : |(deningerArithmeticFEOrientation q).re| = 1 := by
    simp only [deningerArithmeticFEOrientation]
    split_ifs <;> norm_num
  rw [xiCompleteDivisorSignedEnergy, abs_mul, heps, one_mul]
  exact abs_of_nonneg (norm_nonneg _)

theorem xiCompleteDivisorSignedEnergy_reflect (q : XiZeroCopy) :
    xiCompleteDivisorSignedEnergy (xiZeroCopyReflectEquiv q) =
      -xiCompleteDivisorSignedEnergy q := by
  rw [xiCompleteDivisorSignedEnergy, xiCompleteDivisorSignedEnergy,
    deningerArithmeticFEOrientation_reflect, xiCompleteDivisorEnergy,
    xiCompleteDivisorEnergy, xiSpectralPoint_reflect, norm_neg]
  simp only [Complex.neg_re]
  ring

/-- Self-adjoint signed complete-divisor Dirac operator. -/
def xiCompleteDivisorSignedDirac : XiDivisorL2 →ₗ.[ℂ] XiDivisorL2 :=
  maximalRealDiagonal xiCompleteDivisorSignedEnergy

theorem xiCompleteDivisorSignedDirac_isSelfAdjoint :
    IsSelfAdjoint xiCompleteDivisorSignedDirac :=
  maximalRealDiagonal_isSelfAdjoint xiCompleteDivisorSignedEnergy

/-- Reflection preserves the signed maximal domain because it reverses energy but preserves its
absolute value. -/
theorem xiCompleteDivisorReflection_mem_signedDomain
    (x : xiCompleteDivisorSignedDirac.domain) :
    xiCompleteDivisorReflection (x : XiDivisorL2) ∈
      xiCompleteDivisorSignedDirac.domain := by
  change Memℓp
    (fun q : XiZeroCopy =>
      (xiCompleteDivisorSignedEnergy q : ℂ) *
        (x : XiDivisorL2) (xiZeroCopyReflectEquiv q)) 2
  apply HilbertSchmidt.memℓp_of_sq
  have hx : Summable (fun q : XiZeroCopy =>
      ‖(xiCompleteDivisorSignedEnergy q : ℂ) * (x : XiDivisorL2) q‖ ^ 2) := by
    simpa using x.property.summable (by norm_num)
  exact (xiZeroCopyReflectEquiv.summable_iff.mpr hx).congr fun q => by
    simp only [Function.comp_apply, xiCompleteDivisorSignedEnergy_reflect]
    rw [show ((-xiCompleteDivisorSignedEnergy q : ℝ) : ℂ) =
      -(xiCompleteDivisorSignedEnergy q : ℂ) by norm_num,
      neg_mul, norm_neg]

/-- Signed complete divisor is odd under functional-equation reflection. -/
theorem xiCompleteDivisorSignedDirac_reflection_odd
    (x : xiCompleteDivisorSignedDirac.domain) :
    xiCompleteDivisorSignedDirac
        ⟨xiCompleteDivisorReflection (x : XiDivisorL2),
          xiCompleteDivisorReflection_mem_signedDomain x⟩ =
      -xiCompleteDivisorReflection (xiCompleteDivisorSignedDirac x) := by
  ext q
  change (xiCompleteDivisorSignedEnergy q : ℂ) *
      (x : XiDivisorL2) (xiZeroCopyReflectEquiv q) =
    -((xiCompleteDivisorSignedEnergy (xiZeroCopyReflectEquiv q) : ℂ) *
      (x : XiDivisorL2) (xiZeroCopyReflectEquiv q))
  rw [xiCompleteDivisorSignedEnergy_reflect]
  push_cast
  ring

/-- The selected complete logarithmic-derivative series has sum `I` times
the complete positive boundary density at every real point. -/
theorem hasSum_zetaUpperBlaschkeSelectedLogDerivativeSummand_real
    (x : ℝ) :
    HasSum (zetaUpperBlaschkeSelectedLogDerivativeSummand (x : ℂ))
      ((riemannXiUpperBlaschkeBoundaryDensityTotal x : ℂ) * Complex.I) := by

/-- On the real spectral boundary, the complete signed Blaschke logarithmic
derivative is exactly `I` times a convergent nonnegative real sum. -/
theorem riemannXiUpperBlaschkeCompleteLogDerivative_real_eq_density_mul_I

/-- The boundary complete logarithmic derivative has zero real part. -/
theorem riemannXiUpperBlaschkeCompleteLogDerivative_real_re_eq_zero

exactly the complete positive boundary density. -/

resultant is exactly its positive density total. -/

      riemannXiUpperBlaschkeBoundaryDensityTotal x := by

    norm_mul, norm_I, mul_one, norm_real, Real.norm_eq_abs,
    abs_of_nonneg (riemannXiUpperBlaschkeBoundaryDensityTotal_nonneg x)]

/-- Single-invariant boundary rigidity: at every real point, the complete
signed Blaschke logarithmic derivative vanishes exactly when RH holds. -/
theorem riemannXiUpperBlaschkeCompleteLogDerivative_real_eq_zero_iff_rh

      RiemannHypothesis := by

  · intro hzero

      (mul_eq_zero.mp hzero).resolve_right Complex.I_ne_zero
    have hreal : riemannXiUpperBlaschkeBoundaryDensityTotal x = 0 := by

        hRH

    simp

/-- Concrete origin criterion: one fixed boundary value of the complete
signed Blaschke logarithmic derivative vanishes exactly when RH holds. -/
theorem riemannXiUpperBlaschkeCompleteLogDerivative_at_zero_eq_zero_iff_rh :
    riemannXiUpperBlaschkeCompleteLogDerivative 0 = 0 ↔
      RiemannHypothesis := by
  simpa using
    riemannXiUpperBlaschkeCompleteLogDerivative_real_eq_zero_iff_rh 0

is nonzero at every real point. -/

    riemannXiUpperBlaschkeCompleteLogDerivative (x : ℂ) ≠ 0 := by

/-- A subtraction-free formula for the rank of a set in the dual matroid. -/
lemma eRk_dual_add_eRank (M : Matroid α) (X : Set α) (hX : X ⊆ M.E := by aesop_mat) :
    M✶.eRk X + M.eRank = M.eRk (M.E \ X) + X.encard := by
  obtain ⟨I, hI⟩ := M✶.exists_isBasis X
  obtain ⟨B, hB, rfl⟩ := hI.exists_isBasis_inter_eq_of_superset hX
  have hB' : M✶.IsBase B := isBasis_ground_iff.1 hB
  have hd : M.IsBasis (M.E \ B ∩ (M.E \ X)) (M.E \ X) := by
    simpa using hB'.inter_isBasis_iff_compl_inter_isBasis_dual.1 hI
  rw [← hB'.compl_isBase_of_dual.encard_eq_eRank, hI.eRk_eq_encard, hd.eRk_eq_encard,
    ← encard_union_eq (by tauto_set), ← encard_union_eq (by tauto_set)]
  exact congr_arg _ (by tauto_set)

/-- A version of `Matroid.dual_eRk_add_eRank` for non-subsets of the ground set. -/

    M✶.eRk X + M.eRank = M.eRk (M.E \ X) + (X ∩ M.E).encard := by
  rw [← sdiff_inter_self_eq_sdiff, ← eRk_dual_add_eRank .., ← dual_ground, eRk_inter_ground]

@[simp]
lemma eRank_add_eRank_dual (M : Matroid α) : M.eRank + M✶.eRank = M.E.encard := by

/-!
# The semilocal prolate unitary-transport trilemma

A unitary that intertwines both the scaling operator and the number operator of two cyclic pairs
must match their first Jacobi coefficients: the number operator pins the ground state, and unitarity
transports `‖D p₀‖` exactly.  Since the normalized semilocal first Jacobi coefficient contracts
strictly below the archimedean value `1/2`, no such unitary exists.

Intertwining the formal prolate families at two distinct positive parameters is no weaker:
subtracting the two identities recovers the number-operator intertwining, and the remaining identity
transports `⟪p₀, D² p₀⟫ = ‖D p₀‖²`.

## Main results

* `norm_scaling_ground_eq_of_unitary_transport` — a scaling/grading unitary matches `‖D p₀‖`;
* `not_exists_unitary_transport` — hence a strict contraction forbids it;
* `norm_scaling_ground_eq_of_unitary_prolate_transport` — the two-parameter prolate version;
* `semilocal_normalizedSecondMoment_lt_archimedean` — the concrete strict contraction.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace RHTower

open scoped InnerProductSpace

variable {H₁ H₂ : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup H₁] [InnerProductSpace ℂ H₁]
  [NormedAddCommGroup H₂] [InnerProductSpace ℂ H₂]

/-- The ground state is transported up to a unimodular scalar. -/
theorem exists_unimodular_of_ground_transport {N₁ : H₁ →L[ℂ] H₁} {N₂ : H₂ →L[ℂ] H₂}
    {p₁ : H₁} {p₂ : H₂} (hp₁ : ‖p₁‖ = 1) (hp₂ : ‖p₂‖ = 1)
    (hN₁ : N₁ p₁ = 0)
    (hker : ∀ v : H₂, N₂ v = 0 → ∃ c : ℂ, v = c • p₂)
    (U : H₁ ≃ₗᵢ[ℂ] H₂) (hN : ∀ v, U (N₁ v) = N₂ (U v)) :
    ∃ c : ℂ, ‖c‖ = 1 ∧ U p₁ = c • p₂ := by
  have hzero : N₂ (U p₁) = 0 := by
    rw [← hN, hN₁, map_zero]
  obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := hker _ hzero
  refine ⟨c, ?_, hc⟩
  have hnorm : ‖U p₁‖ = 1 := by rw [U.norm_map, hp₁]
  rw [hc, norm_smul, hp₂, mul_one] at hnorm
  exact hnorm

/-- **A scaling/grading unitary matches the first Jacobi coefficient.** -/
theorem norm_scaling_ground_eq_of_unitary_transport {D₁ N₁ : H₁ →L[ℂ] H₁}
    {D₂ N₂ : H₂ →L[ℂ] H₂} {p₁ : H₁} {p₂ : H₂} (hp₁ : ‖p₁‖ = 1) (hp₂ : ‖p₂‖ = 1)
    (hN₁ : N₁ p₁ = 0)
    (hker : ∀ v : H₂, N₂ v = 0 → ∃ c : ℂ, v = c • p₂)
    (U : H₁ ≃ₗᵢ[ℂ] H₂)
    (hD : ∀ v, U (D₁ v) = D₂ (U v)) (hN : ∀ v, U (N₁ v) = N₂ (U v)) :
    ‖D₁ p₁‖ = ‖D₂ p₂‖ := by
  obtain ⟨c, hc1, hc⟩ := exists_unimodular_of_ground_transport hp₁ hp₂ hN₁ hker U hN
  calc ‖D₁ p₁‖ = ‖U (D₁ p₁)‖ := (U.norm_map _).symm
    _ = ‖D₂ (U p₁)‖ := by rw [hD]
    _ = ‖D₂ (c • p₂)‖ := by rw [hc]
    _ = ‖D₂ p₂‖ := by rw [map_smul, norm_smul, hc1, one_mul]

/-- **The transport no-go.**  A strict contraction of the first Jacobi coefficient rules out every
simultaneous scaling/grading unitary. -/
theorem not_exists_unitary_transport {D₁ N₁ : H₁ →L[ℂ] H₁}
    {D₂ N₂ : H₂ →L[ℂ] H₂} {p₁ : H₁} {p₂ : H₂} (hp₁ : ‖p₁‖ = 1) (hp₂ : ‖p₂‖ = 1)
    (hN₁ : N₁ p₁ = 0)
    (hker : ∀ v : H₂, N₂ v = 0 → ∃ c : ℂ, v = c • p₂)
    (hlt : ‖D₂ p₂‖ < ‖D₁ p₁‖) :
    ¬ ∃ U : H₁ ≃ₗᵢ[ℂ] H₂,
        (∀ v, U (D₁ v) = D₂ (U v)) ∧ (∀ v, U (N₁ v) = N₂ (U v)) := by
  rintro ⟨U, hD, hN⟩
  have := norm_scaling_ground_eq_of_unitary_transport hp₁ hp₂ hN₁ hker U hD hN
  linarith

/-! ### The two-parameter prolate version -/

/-- The formal prolate operator `-D² + λ² N`. -/
def prolateOp (D N : H₁ →L[ℂ] H₁) (lam : ℂ) : H₁ →L[ℂ] H₁ :=
  -(D.comp D) + (lam ^ 2) • N

/-- Two distinct prolate parameters recover the number-operator intertwining. -/
theorem number_transport_of_two_prolate {D₁ N₁ : H₁ →L[ℂ] H₁} {D₂ N₂ : H₂ →L[ℂ] H₂}
    {lam mu : ℂ} (hne : lam ^ 2 ≠ mu ^ 2) (U : H₁ ≃ₗᵢ[ℂ] H₂)
    (hlam : ∀ v, U (prolateOp D₁ N₁ lam v) = prolateOp D₂ N₂ lam (U v))
    (hmu : ∀ v, U (prolateOp D₁ N₁ mu v) = prolateOp D₂ N₂ mu (U v)) :
    (∀ v, U (N₁ v) = N₂ (U v)) ∧ (∀ v, U (D₁ (D₁ v)) = D₂ (D₂ (U v))) := by
  have hN : ∀ v, U (N₁ v) = N₂ (U v) := by
    intro v
    have h1 := hlam v
    have h2 := hmu v
    simp only [prolateOp, add_apply, neg_apply,
      smul_apply, ContinuousLinearMap.comp_apply] at h1 h2
    rw [map_add, map_neg, map_smul] at h1 h2
    have key : (lam ^ 2 - mu ^ 2) • U (N₁ v) = (lam ^ 2 - mu ^ 2) • N₂ (U v) := by
      rw [sub_smul, sub_smul]
      linear_combination (norm := module) h1 - h2
    exact smul_right_injective _ (sub_ne_zero.mpr hne) key
  refine ⟨hN, fun v => ?_⟩
  have h1 := hlam v
  simp only [prolateOp, add_apply, neg_apply,
    smul_apply, ContinuousLinearMap.comp_apply] at h1
  rw [map_add, map_neg, map_smul, hN v] at h1
  have h2 : -U (D₁ (D₁ v)) = -(D₂ (D₂ (U v))) := add_right_cancel h1
  exact neg_injective h2

/-- **The two-parameter prolate transport also matches the first Jacobi coefficient.** -/
theorem norm_scaling_ground_eq_of_unitary_prolate_transport {D₁ N₁ : H₁ →L[ℂ] H₁}
    {D₂ N₂ : H₂ →L[ℂ] H₂} {p₁ : H₁} {p₂ : H₂} {lam mu : ℂ}
    (hp₁ : ‖p₁‖ = 1) (hp₂ : ‖p₂‖ = 1) (hN₁ : N₁ p₁ = 0)
    (hsa₁ : ∀ x y : H₁, ⟪D₁ x, y⟫_ℂ = ⟪x, D₁ y⟫_ℂ)
    (hsa₂ : ∀ x y : H₂, ⟪D₂ x, y⟫_ℂ = ⟪x, D₂ y⟫_ℂ)

∈ M.E := by aesop_mat) :
    M.eRk {e} = 1 :=
  (M.isNonloop_of_loopless he).eRk_eq

@[simp]
lemma eRk_singleton_le (M : Matroid α) (e : α) : M.eRk {e} ≤ 1 :=
  (M.eRk_le_encard {e}).trans_eq <| encard_singleton e

@[simp]
lemma eRk_singleton_eq_one_iff {e : α} : M.eRk {e} = 1 ↔ M.IsNonloop e := by
  refine ⟨fun h ↦ ?_, fun h ↦ h.eRk_eq⟩
  rwa [← indep_singleton, indep_iff_eRk_eq_encard_of_finite (by simp), encard_singleton]

lemma eRk_eq_one_iff (hX : X ⊆ M.E := by aesop_mat) :
    M.eRk X = 1 ↔ ∃ e ∈ X, M.IsNonloop e ∧ X ⊆ M.closure {e} := by
  refine ⟨?_, fun ⟨e, heX, he, hXe⟩ ↦ ?_⟩
  · obtain ⟨I, hI⟩ := M.exists_isBasis X
    rw [hI.eRk_eq_encard, encard_eq_one]
    rintro ⟨e, rfl⟩
    exact ⟨e, singleton_subset_iff.1 hI.subset, indep_singleton.1 hI.indep, hI.subset_closure⟩
  rw [← he.eRk_eq]
  exact ((M.eRk_mono hXe).trans (M.eRk_closure_eq _).le).antisymm
    (M.eRk_mono (singleton_subset_iff.2 heX))

lemma eRk_le_one_iff [M.Nonempty] (hX : X ⊆ M.E := by aesop_mat) :
    M.eRk X ≤ 1 ↔ ∃ e ∈ M.E, X ⊆ M.closure {e} := by
  refine ⟨fun h ↦ ?_, fun ⟨e, _, he⟩ ↦ ?_⟩
  · obtain ⟨I, hI⟩ := M.exists_isBasis X
    rw [hI.eRk_eq_encard, encard_le_one_iff_eq] at h
    obtain (rfl | ⟨e, rfl⟩) := h
    · obtain ⟨e, he⟩ := M.ground_nonempty
      exact ⟨e, he, hI.subset_closure.trans ((M.closure_subset_closure (empty_subset _)))⟩
    exact ⟨e, hI.indep.subset_ground rfl,  hI.subset_closure⟩
  refine (M.eRk_mono he).trans ?_
  rw [eRk_closure_eq, ← encard_singleton e]
  exact M.eRk_le_encard {e}

/-! ### Spanning Sets -/

lemma Spanning.eRk_eq (hX : M.Spanning X) : M.eRk X = M.eRank := by
  obtain ⟨B, hB⟩ := M.exists_isBasis X
  exact (M.eRk_le_eRank X).antisymm <| by
    rw [← hB.encard_eq_eRk, ← (hB.isBase_of_spanning hX).encard_eq_eRank]

lemma spanning_iff_eRk_le' [RankFinite M] : M.Spanning X ↔ M.eRank ≤ M.eRk X ∧ X ⊆ M.E := by
  refine ⟨fun h ↦ ⟨h.eRk_eq.symm.le, h.subset_ground⟩, fun ⟨h, hX⟩ ↦ ?_⟩
  obtain ⟨I, hI⟩ := M.exists_isBasis X
  exact (hI.indep.isBase_of_eRk_ge
    hI.indep.finite (h.trans hI.eRk_eq_eRk.symm.le)).spanning_of_superset hI.subset

lemma spanning_iff_eRk_le [RankFinite M] (hX : X ⊆ M.E := by aesop_mat) :
    M.Spanning X ↔ M.eRank ≤ M.eRk X := by
  rw [spanning_iff_eRk_le', and_iff_left hX]

lemma Spanning.eRank_restrict (hX : M.Spanning X) : (M ↾ X).eRank = M.eRank := by
  rw [eRank_def, restrict_ground_eq, restrict_eRk_eq _ rfl.subset, hX.eRk_eq]

/-! ### Constructions -/

@[simp]
lemma eRank_map {β : Type*} {f : α → β} (M : Matroid α) (hf : InjOn f M.E) :
    (M.map f hf).eRank = M.eRank := by
  obtain ⟨B, hB⟩ := M.exists_isBase
  rw [← (hB.map hf).encard_eq_eRank, ← hB.encard_eq_eRank, (hf.mono hB.subset_ground).encard_image]

@[simp]
lemma eRk_map {β : Type*} {f : α → β} (M : Matroid α) (hf : InjOn f M.E)
    (hX : X ⊆ M.E := by aesop_mat) : (M.map f hf).eRk (f '' X) = M.eRk X := by
  obtain ⟨I, hI⟩ := M.exists_isBasis X
  rw [hI.eRk_eq_encard, (hI.map hf).eRk_eq_encard, (hf.mono hI.indep.subset_ground).encard_image]

@[simp]
lemma eRk_comap {β : Type*} {f : α → β} (M : Matroid β) (X : Set α) :
    (M.comap f).eRk X = M.eRk (f '' X) := by
  obtain ⟨I, hI⟩ := (M.comap f).exists_isBasis' X
  obtain ⟨hI', hinj, -⟩ := comap_isBasis'_iff.1 hI

@[simp]

  obtain ⟨I, hI⟩ := (loopyOn Y).exists_isBasis' X

@[simp]
lemma eRank_loopyOn (X : Set α) : (loopyOn X).eRank = 0 := by
  rw [eRank_def, eRk_loopyOn]

lemma eRank_eq_zero_iff : M.eRank = 0 ↔ M = loopyOn M.E := by
  refine ⟨fun h ↦ closure_empty_eq_ground_iff.1 ?_, fun h ↦ by rw [h, eRank_loopyOn]⟩
  obtain ⟨B, hB⟩ := M.exists_isBase
  rw [← hB.encard_eq_eRank, encard_eq_zero] at h

  rw [eRank_eq_zero_iff, emptyOn_ground, loopyOn_empty]

@[simp]
lemma eRank_freeOn (X : Set α) : (freeOn X).eRank = X.encard := by
  rw [eRank_def, freeOn_ground, (freeOn_indep_iff.2 rfl.subset).eRk_eq_encard]

lemma eRk_freeOn (hXY : X ⊆ Y) : (freeOn Y).eRk X = X.encard := by
  obtain ⟨I, hI⟩ := (freeOn Y).exists_isBasis X

  (hB.compl_isBase_dual).encard_eq_eRank

/-- A subtraction-free formula for the rank of a set in the dual matroid. -/
lemma eRk_dual_add_eRank (M : Matroid α) (X : Set α) (hX : X ⊆ M.E := by aesop_mat) :

import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Rayleigh

/-!
# Scalar renormalization of Rayleigh excess

Adding a real scalar multiple of the identity shifts every Rayleigh value and every spectral
energy by the same scalar.  It therefore leaves the spectral gap, Rayleigh excess, and their ratio
unchanged.  This is the exact consumer for the universal `log c` identity term in the CCM
archimedean form: only the scalar-renormalized remainder can affect ground-vector selection.
-/

open scoped InnerProductSpace

namespace RHTower

variable {𝕜 E : Type*} [RCLike 𝕜]
variable [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 E]

/-- A real scalar identity shift adds that scalar to every nonzero Rayleigh quotient. -/
theorem rayleighQuotient_add_real_smul_id
    (T : E →L[𝕜] E) (r : ℝ) (x : E) (hx : x ≠ 0) :
    (T + (r : 𝕜) • ContinuousLinearMap.id 𝕜 E).rayleighQuotient x =
      T.rayleighQuotient x + r := by
  rw [ContinuousLinearMap.rayleighQuotient_add]
  simp only [ContinuousLinearMap.rayleighQuotient,
    ContinuousLinearMap.reApplyInnerSelf_apply, _root_.smul_apply,
    ContinuousLinearMap.id_apply]
  rw [inner_smul_left, RCLike.conj_ofReal, RCLike.re_ofReal_mul,
    inner_self_eq_norm_sq]
  field_simp

/-- Subtracting the correspondingly shifted ground energy removes a scalar identity shift from
the Rayleigh excess exactly. -/
theorem rayleighExcess_add_real_smul_id
    (T : E →L[𝕜] E) (r epsilon : ℝ) (x : E) (hx : x ≠ 0) :
    (T + (r : 𝕜) • ContinuousLinearMap.id 𝕜 E).rayleighQuotient x -
        (epsilon + r) =
      T.rayleighQuotient x - epsilon := by
  rw [rayleighQuotient_add_real_smul_id T r x hx]
  ring

/-- A common scalar shift cancels from a spectral gap. -/
theorem spectralGap_add_cancel (epsilon₀ epsilon₁ r : ℝ) :
    (epsilon₁ + r) - (epsilon₀ + r) = epsilon₁ - epsilon₀ := by
  ring

/-- The dimensionless Rayleigh-excess-to-gap ratio is exactly invariant under a real scalar
identity shift. -/
theorem rayleighExcessRatio_add_real_smul_id
    (T : E →L[𝕜] E) (r epsilon₀ epsilon₁ : ℝ) (x : E) (hx : x ≠ 0) :
    ((T + (r : 𝕜) • ContinuousLinearMap.id 𝕜 E).rayleighQuotient x -
          (epsilon₀ + r)) /
        ((epsilon₁ + r) - (epsilon₀ + r)) =
      (T.rayleighQuotient x - epsilon₀) / (epsilon₁ - epsilon₀) := by
  rw [rayleighQuotient_add_real_smul_id T r x hx]
  ring

end RHTower

import GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower.ConstrainedProlateEvaluationIdentity

/-!
# Centre value of a compensated zero-integral tail

A tail `∑ t_m e_m` is corrected to zero integral by subtracting a multiple of the ground mode,
`r = ∑ t_m e_m − (L/ℓ₀) e₀` with `L = ∑ t_m ℓ_m`.  Its centre value is then not the naive
`∑ t_m e_m(0)` but

`r(0) = ∑ t_m e_m(0) (1 − χ_m/χ₀)`,

because each integral coordinate is its own eigenvalue times its own centre value.  The correction
factor rewrites as

`1 − χ_m/χ₀ = (d_m − d₀)/(χ₀(χ₀ + χ_m))`,   `d_j = 1 − χ_j²`,

so the compensation contributes a factor of the *leakage difference* rather than a reciprocal
leakage.  That is the point of the construction: no `1/d_m` appears.

Both statements are exact algebra over `ℂ`; the arithmetic input is only the evaluation identity
`ℓ_j = χ_j e_j(0)`, which is proved separately for genuine time-band eigenmodes.
-/

open Finset

namespace RHTower

/-- The compensation factor in terms of the leakages `d = 1 - χ²`. -/
theorem one_sub_div_eq_leakage_difference {χ₀ χ : ℂ} (h₀ : χ₀ ≠ 0) (hsum : χ₀ + χ ≠ 0) :
    1 - χ / χ₀ = ((1 - χ ^ 2) - (1 - χ₀ ^ 2)) / (χ₀ * (χ₀ + χ)) := by
  field_simp
  ring

/-- **Compensated centre value.**  Writing each integral coordinate as `ℓ = χ · e(0)`, the
zero-integral correction turns the centre value into a sum weighted by `1 - χ_m/χ₀`. -/
theorem compensated_centre_value {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι)
    (t χ e : ι → ℂ) {χ₀ e₀ : ℂ} (hχ₀ : χ₀ ≠ 0) (he₀ : e₀ ≠ 0) :
    (∑ m ∈ s, t m * e m)
        - ((∑ m ∈ s, t m * (χ m * e m)) / (χ₀ * e₀)) * e₀
      = ∑ m ∈ s, t m * e m * (1 - χ m / χ₀) := by
  have hsplit : ∑ m ∈ s, t m * e m * (1 - χ m / χ₀)
      = (∑ m ∈ s, t m * e m) - (∑ m ∈ s, t m * (χ m * e m)) / χ₀ := by
    rw [Finset.sum_div, ← Finset.sum_sub_distrib]
    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    intro m _
    field_simp
  rw [hsplit]
  congr 1
  field_simp

/-- The compensation is exactly what makes the corrected tail have zero integral. -/
theorem compensated_integral_eq_zero {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι)
    (t ℓ : ι → ℂ) {ℓ₀ : ℂ} (hℓ₀ : ℓ₀ ≠ 0) :
    (∑ m ∈ s, t m * ℓ m) - ((∑ m ∈ s, t m * ℓ m) / ℓ₀) * ℓ₀ = 0 := by
  field_simp
  ring

/-- **Specialization to genuine time-band eigenmodes.**  The hypotheses are only that the ground
eigenvalue and ground centre value are nonzero; the identity `ℓ = χ · e(0)` is supplied by
`timeBandEigenSourceIntegral_eq_mul_pointwiseSource_zero`. -/
theorem compensated_centre_value_timeBand {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι) (t : ι → ℂ)
    {a : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a)
    (f : ι → evenSubspace) (χ : ι → ℂ) (hχ : ∀ i, χ i ≠ 0)
    (heig : ∀ i, evenTimeBandFourier a (f i) = χ i • f i)
    (f₀ : evenSubspace) (χ₀ : ℂ) (hχ₀ : χ₀ ≠ 0)
    (heig₀ : evenTimeBandFourier a f₀ = χ₀ • f₀)
    (he₀ : timeBandEigenPointwiseSource a f₀ χ₀ hχ₀ heig₀ 0 ≠ 0) :
    (∑ m ∈ s, t m * timeBandEigenPointwiseSource a (f m) (χ m) (hχ m) (heig m) 0)
        - ((∑ m ∈ s, t m * timeBandEigenSourceIntegral a (f m) (χ m) (hχ m) (heig m))
            / timeBandEigenSourceIntegral a f₀ χ₀ hχ₀ heig₀)
          * timeBandEigenPointwiseSource a f₀ χ₀ hχ₀ heig₀ 0
      = ∑ m ∈ s, t m * timeBandEigenPointwiseSource a (f m) (χ m) (hχ m) (heig m) 0
          * (1 - χ m / χ₀) := by
  have hL : ∀ i : ι, timeBandEigenSourceIntegral a (f i) (χ i) (hχ i) (heig i)
      = χ i * timeBandEigenPointwiseSource a (f i) (χ i) (hχ i) (heig i) 0 := fun i =>
    timeBandEigenSourceIntegral_eq_mul_pointwiseSource_zero a ha (f i) (χ i) (hχ i) (heig i)
  have hL₀ : timeBandEigenSourceIntegral a f₀ χ₀ hχ₀ heig₀
      = χ₀ * timeBandEigenPointwiseSource a f₀ χ₀ hχ₀ heig₀ 0 :=
    timeBandEigenSourceIntegral_eq_mul_pointwiseSource_zero a ha f₀ χ₀ hχ₀ heig₀
  have hsum : ∑ m ∈ s, t m * timeBandEigenSourceIntegral a (f m) (χ m) (hχ m) (heig m)
      = ∑ m ∈ s, t m * (χ m *
          timeBandEigenPointwiseSource a (f m) (χ m) (hχ m) (heig m) 0) := by
    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    intro m _
    rw [hL m]
  rw [hsum, hL₀]
  exact compensated_centre_value s t χ
    (fun m => timeBandEigenPointwiseSource a (f m) (χ m) (hχ m) (heig m) 0) hχ₀ he₀

end RHTower

inverse-tilted source.  No computation is used.

# Xi endpoint curvature is a boundary value of the central moment germ

- **ID:** `xi-endpoint-central-moment-boundary-value`
- **Stage:** 3-formalized
- **Type:** theorem / exact source-value relation
- **Scientific status:** `[PROVED HERE] [NOT NEW SCIENTIFIC KNOWLEDGE]`

## Statement

Let

\[
G_\Xi(z)=\sum_{n\ge 0}M_nz^{2n}
\]

be the centered reciprocal-square moment germ, equivalently the Taylor germ of the normalized
completed prime--Gamma relative trace.  Then the source-pure endpoint height gap places every
reciprocal-square coordinate inside the unit disk, so the series and divisor resolvent remain
absolutely convergent at `z=i/2`.  At that point the reciprocal-square resolvent term is exactly
the FE--Schwarz endpoint cross term.  Therefore

/-- Public RSA-2048 resource-estimate certificate. The correctness part is a
source-level factor-return certificate; the resource tuple is the pinned
source-backed logical estimate recorded in this namespace. The factor-return
route is the Shor order-finding reduction, while the numerical tuple is the GE19
RSA-2048 estimate [Sho95, source.tex:1124-1148] [GE19, main.tex:70-79,
211-216, 888-889, 1785-1788]. -/
private structure PublicSourceEstimateCertificate
    {N : ℕ} (model : ShorFactoring.SemiprimeFactorModel N) where
  /-- Factor-return certificate supplied to the public endpoint. -/
  factorReturn : ShorFactoring.ProbabilisticFactorReturnCertificate model

/-- Build the RSA-2048 terminal Shor-style success certificate from source
pieces. This is the terminal wrapper around the generic Shor constructor: the
random-base factor-yield route, order-recovery rational lower-bound fields,
repetition model, and retry-amplification certificate are assembled before the
RSA-2048 source-estimate endpoint consumes the success certificate [Sho95,
source.tex:1124-1148, source.tex:1132-1169, source.tex:1614-1663,
source.tex:1647-1663]. -/
private def retrySuccessCertificateOfSourcePieces
    (input : InputClass)
    {retry : RetryMultiplierSpec}
    {orderRecoverySuccessNumerator orderRecoverySuccessDenominator : ℕ}
    (good :
      ShorFactoring.SemiprimeFactorModel.RandomBaseGoodEventLowerBound
        input.model)
    (sample : ShorFactoring.RandomBaseUnitSample input.model)
    (order : ℕ)
    (route :
      ShorFactoring.HalfOrderGcdInput input.modulus sample.baseResidue order)
    (orderRecoverySource :
      ShorStyle.OrderRecoveryRationalFieldCertificate order
        orderRecoverySuccessNumerator orderRecoverySuccessDenominator)
    (repetition : RetryMultiplierSpec.RepetitionModel retry)
    (amplification : ShorStyle.RetryAmplificationCertificate retry) :
    ShorStyle.RetrySuccessCertificate input.model retry := by
  let factorYield :=
    ShorStyle.RandomBaseFactorYieldCertificate.ofPublicGoodEventRoute
      good sample order route
  exact ShorStyle.RetrySuccessCertificate.ofSourcePieces factorYield
    orderRecoverySource repetition amplification

/-- Public endpoint for the RSA-2048 logical-resource estimate. This proves the
stored source-backed tuple and the explicit classical arithmetic count attached
to the factor-return certificate. The quantum tuple remains a source-backed
estimate rather than an exact-resource theorem. The external correctness
certificate follows the Shor order-finding route [Sho95, source.tex:1124-1148,
1630-1663], while the resource tuple is GE19's source estimate [GE19,
main.tex:70-79, 211-216, 888-889, 1785-1788]. -/
private theorem main_sourceEstimate
    {N : ℕ} {model : ShorFactoring.SemiprimeFactorModel N}
    (cert : PublicSourceEstimateCertificate model) :
    (cert.factorReturn.output.output = model.leftFactor ∨
        cert.factorReturn.output.output = model.rightFactor) ∧
      2 * cert.factorReturn.successDenominator ≤
        3 * cert.factorReturn.successNumerator ∧
      logicalResourceEstimate.logicalQubits = 6190 ∧
      logicalResourceEstimate.toffoliGates = 2700000000 ∧
      logicalResourceEstimate.circuitDepth = 2140000000 ∧
      classicalArithmeticOpsPerRun = 12302 ∧
      sourceEstimateEnvelope.fields = logicalResourceEstimate ∧
      sourceEstimateEnvelope.readyForFinalStatement = false :=
  ⟨cert.factorReturn.output_mem_declared_factors,
    cert.factorReturn.successAtLeastTwoThirds,
    logicalResourceEstimate_logicalQubits,
    logicalResourceEstimate_toffoliGates,
    logicalResourceEstimate_circuitDepth,
    classicalArithmeticOpsPerRun_eq,
    rfl,
    sourceEstimateEnvelope_not_ready⟩

/-- Second CCM endpoint cyclic morphism `ε₁ⁿ`, induced by adelic Haar trace. -/
def ccmRationalAdelicEpsilonOneCyclicHom :
    CyclicModule.Hom CCMRationalAdelicSourceCyclicModule
      (scalarConstantCyclicModule (R := ℂ)) :=
  cyclicBarTraceCyclicHom ccmRationalAdelicEpsilonOne
    ccmRationalAdelicEpsilonOne_isTrace

@[simp]
theorem ccmRationalAdelicEpsilonOneCyclicHom_app (n : ℕ) :
    ccmRationalAdelicEpsilonOneCyclicHom.simplicial.app (.op (.mk n)) =
      ModuleCat.ofHom
        (cyclicBarTraceAugmentation ccmRationalAdelicEpsilonOne n) :=
  rfl

/-- First endpoint restricted to the correct nonunital cyclic source. -/
def ccmRationalAdelicNonunitalEpsilonZeroCyclicHom :
    CyclicModule.Hom CCMRationalAdelicNonunitalSourceCyclicModule
      (scalarConstantCyclicModule (R := ℂ)) :=
  CyclicModule.Hom.comp ccmRationalAdelicNonunitalSourceCyclicInclusion
    ccmRationalAdelicEpsilonZeroCyclicHom

/-- Haar endpoint restricted to the correct nonunital cyclic source. -/
def ccmRationalAdelicNonunitalEpsilonOneCyclicHom :
    CyclicModule.Hom CCMRationalAdelicNonunitalSourceCyclicModule
      (scalarConstantCyclicModule (R := ℂ)) :=
  CyclicModule.Hom.comp ccmRationalAdelicNonunitalSourceCyclicInclusion
    ccmRationalAdelicEpsilonOneCyclicHom

/-- Genuine reduced CCM cyclic source: first remove the adjoined scalar unit, then impose
`ker ε₀ ∩ ker ε₁`. -/
abbrev CCMRationalAdelicReducedSourceCyclicModule : CyclicModule ℂ :=
  ccmRationalAdelicNonunitalEpsilonZeroCyclicHom.doubleKernel
    ccmRationalAdelicNonunitalEpsilonOneCyclicHom

/-- Canonical inclusion of the reduced cyclic source into the full source. -/
def ccmRationalAdelicReducedSourceCyclicInclusion :
  CyclicModule.Hom CCMRationalAdelicReducedSourceCyclicModule
      CCMRationalAdelicSourceCyclicModule :=
  CyclicModule.Hom.comp
    (ccmRationalAdelicNonunitalEpsilonZeroCyclicHom.doubleKernelInclusion
      ccmRationalAdelicNonunitalEpsilonOneCyclicHom)
    ccmRationalAdelicNonunitalSourceCyclicInclusion

/-- Membership in the reduced degree is exactly simultaneous vanishing of both endpoints. -/
theorem ccmRationalAdelicReducedSourceCyclicModule_mem_iff
    (n : ℕ)
    (x : CCMRationalAdelicNonunitalSourceCyclicModule.simplicial.obj
      (.op (.mk n))) :
    x ∈ ccmRationalAdelicNonunitalEpsilonZeroCyclicHom.doubleKernelSubmodule
        ccmRationalAdelicNonunitalEpsilonOneCyclicHom (.op (.mk n)) ↔
      ccmRationalAdelicNonunitalEpsilonZeroCyclicHom.simplicial.app
          (.op (.mk n)) x = 0 ∧
        ccmRationalAdelicNonunitalEpsilonOneCyclicHom.simplicial.app
          (.op (.mk n)) x = 0 :=
  CyclicModule.Hom.mem_doubleKernelSubmodule_iff _ _ _ _

theorem laplaceMoments_eq_top_of_laplaceMass_eq_top (ν : Measure ℝ) {a t : ℝ} (ht : 0 ≤ t)
    (h : laplaceMass ν (a - t) = ⊤) :
    (∑' k : ℕ, ENNReal.ofReal (t ^ k / (k.factorial : ℝ)) * laplaceMoment ν a k) = ⊤ := by
  rw [← landau_exchange ν a t ht]; exact h

section Monotone

/-- The transform of a nonnegative measure is antitone in the abscissa on `(0,∞)`. -/
theorem laplaceMass_antitone (ν : Measure ℝ) {σ τ : ℝ} (h : σ ≤ τ) :
    laplaceMass ν τ ≤ laplaceMass ν σ := by
  refine MeasureTheory.lintegral_mono_ae ?_
  filter_upwards [self_mem_ae_restrict (measurableSet_Ioi (a := (0 : ℝ)))] with u hu
  have hu' : (0 : ℝ) < u := hu
  exact ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal (Real.exp_le_exp.mpr (by nlinarith))

end Monotone

section Abscissa

/-- `IsAbscissa ν c` says that `c` is the abscissa of convergence of the Laplace transform of the
nonnegative measure `ν`: the transform converges strictly to the right of `c` and diverges
strictly to the left. -/
def IsAbscissa (ν : Measure ℝ) (c : ℝ) : Prop :=
  (∀ σ : ℝ, c < σ → laplaceMass ν σ ≠ ⊤) ∧ (∀ σ : ℝ, σ < c → laplaceMass ν σ = ⊤)

/-- **The Taylor radius at a real point equals the distance to the abscissa: convergence side.**
For `a` to the right of the abscissa `c`, the moment series at `a` converges for every radius
parameter below `a - c`. -/
theorem moments_ne_top_of_lt_abscissaDist {ν : Measure ℝ} {c a t : ℝ}
    (hc : IsAbscissa ν c) (ht : 0 ≤ t) (hlt : t < a - c) :
    (∑' k : ℕ, ENNReal.ofReal (t ^ k / (k.factorial : ℝ)) * laplaceMoment ν a k) ≠ ⊤ := by
  rw [← landau_exchange ν a t ht]
  exact hc.1 (a - t) (by linarith)

/-- **The Taylor radius at a real point equals the distance to the abscissa: divergence side.**
Beyond `a - c` the moment series diverges, so the radius is exactly `a - c` and the transform has
no analytic continuation to a disc about `a` of radius larger than `a - c`. -/
theorem moments_eq_top_of_gt_abscissaDist {ν : Measure ℝ} {c a t : ℝ}
    (hc : IsAbscissa ν c) (ht : 0 ≤ t) (hgt : a - c < t) :
    (∑' k : ℕ, ENNReal.ofReal (t ^ k / (k.factorial : ℝ)) * laplaceMoment ν a k) = ⊤ := by
  rw [← landau_exchange ν a t ht]
  exact hc.2 (a - t) (by linarith)

end Abscissa

section Domination

/-- The modulus of the complex Laplace kernel is the real kernel at the same real part. -/
theorem norm_cexp_neg_mul (z : ℂ) (u : ℝ) :
    ‖Complex.exp (-z * (u : ℂ))‖ = Real.exp (-z.re * u) := by
  rw [Complex.norm_exp]
  congr 1
  simp [Complex.mul_re]

/-- **Domination by the real point.**  For a nonnegative measure, the complex Laplace transform is
bounded in modulus by the real transform at the same real part.  This is the inequality
`|N(z)| ≤ N(Re z)`, which forces an entire transform of a nonnegative measure with vanishing real
limits to be a bounded entire function, hence constant. -/
theorem norm_complexLaplace_le (ν : Measure ℝ) (z : ℂ) :
    ‖∫ u in Ioi (0 : ℝ), Complex.exp (-z * (u : ℂ)) ∂ν‖
      ≤ ∫ u in Ioi (0 : ℝ), Real.exp (-z.re * u) ∂ν := by
  refine (norm_integral_le_integral_norm _).trans_eq ?_
  exact integral_congr_ae (Eventually.of_forall fun u => norm_cexp_neg_mul z u)

end Domination

/-!
# The 2026 discrete Möbius--Laplace criterion frontier

Liflandsky (`arXiv:2607.09797`) studies

`Phi(exp(-x)) = sum mu(n) * exp(-n*x)`.

The paper proves unconditionally that an `O(x^(-1/2))` bound at zero implies RH.  Its mechanism is
that the Mellin transform, initially `Gamma(s) / zeta(s)` on `Re s > 1`, then extends analytically
to `Re s > 1/2`; the zero-free Gamma numerator forbids a zeta zero there.  The converse in the
paper uses additional simple-zero and zero-sum hypotheses and is not imported as an unconditional
fact.

This file constructs the exact series, proves its absolute convergence and continuity for every
`x > 0`, establishes its exponential tail, identifies its Mellin transform with
`Gamma(s) / zeta(s)` on `Re s > 1`, and formalizes the paper's analytic-continuation argument.
Consequently the source half-power decay implies RH as an unconditional Lean theorem.  The theorem
does not assert that the open decay premise holds.
-/

/-- A term of Liflandsky's discrete Laplace transform.  The `n = 0` term vanishes because
the arithmetic Möbius function is zero there, so this equals the paper's sum from `n = 1`. -/
def mobiusDiscreteLaplaceTerm (x : ℝ) (n : ℕ) : ℂ :=
  ((ArithmeticFunction.moebius n : ℤ) : ℂ) *
    Complex.exp (-((n : ℝ) * x : ℝ))

/-- Liflandsky's discrete Möbius--Laplace transform `sum mu(n) exp(-n*x)`. -/
def mobiusDiscreteLaplaceTransform (x : ℝ) : ℂ :=
  ∑' n : ℕ, mobiusDiscreteLaplaceTerm x n

/-- The source series is absolutely summable at every positive Laplace scale. -/
theorem summable_mobiusDiscreteLaplaceTerm {x : ℝ} (hx : 0 < x) :
    Summable (mobiusDiscreteLaplaceTerm x) := by
  apply Summable.of_norm
  refine Summable.of_nonneg_of_le (fun n => norm_nonneg _) (fun n => ?_)
    (summable_pow_mul_exp_neg 0 hx)
  rw [mobiusDiscreteLaplaceTerm, norm_mul, Complex.norm_exp]
  have hmu : ‖((ArithmeticFunction.moebius n : ℤ) : ℂ)‖ ≤ 1 := by
    rw [Complex.norm_intCast]
    exact_mod_cast ArithmeticFunction.abs_moebius_le_one (n := n)
  have hexp : 0 ≤ Real.exp (-((n : ℝ) * x)) := (Real.exp_pos _).le
  simpa using mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hmu hexp

/-- The defining series converges to the named transform at every positive scale. -/
theorem mobiusDiscreteLaplaceTerm_hasSum {x : ℝ} (hx : 0 < x) :
    HasSum (mobiusDiscreteLaplaceTerm x) (mobiusDiscreteLaplaceTransform x) :=
  (summable_mobiusDiscreteLaplaceTerm hx).hasSum

/-- At positive real scale, the Möbius--Laplace transform is real. -/
theorem mobiusDiscreteLaplaceTransform_im_eq_zero {x : ℝ} (hx : 0 < x) :
    (mobiusDiscreteLaplaceTransform x).im = 0 := by
  have hsum := summable_mobiusDiscreteLaplaceTerm hx
  have hmap := hsum.hasSum.map Complex.imCLM Complex.imCLM.continuous
  have hterm (n : ℕ) : (mobiusDiscreteLaplaceTerm x n).im = 0 := by
    have hexpim :
        (Complex.exp (-((n : ℝ) * x : ℝ))).im = 0 :=
      by simpa using Complex.exp_ofReal_im (-((n : ℝ) * x))
    rw [mobiusDiscreteLaplaceTerm, Complex.mul_im]
    change ((ArithmeticFunction.moebius n : ℤ) : ℂ).re *
        (Complex.exp (-((n : ℝ) * x : ℝ))).im +
      ((ArithmeticFunction.moebius n : ℤ) : ℂ).im *
        (Complex.exp (-((n : ℝ) * x : ℝ))).re = 0
    rw [hexpim]
    simp
  change HasSum (fun n => (mobiusDiscreteLaplaceTerm x n).im)
    (mobiusDiscreteLaplaceTransform x).im at hmap
  have hfun : (fun n => (mobiusDiscreteLaplaceTerm x n).im) =
      (fun _ : ℕ => (0 : ℝ)) := funext hterm
  rw [hfun] at hmap
  exact hmap.unique hasSum_zero

/-- The Möbius--Laplace transform is continuous on the positive real axis. -/
theorem continuousOn_mobiusDiscreteLaplaceTransform :
    ContinuousOn mobiusDiscreteLaplaceTransform (Ioi 0) := by
  intro x hx
  let a : ℝ := x / 2
  have hxpos : 0 < x := hx
  have ha : 0 < a := by dsimp [a]; linarith
  have hax : a < x := by dsimp [a]; linarith
  have hmajor : Summable (fun n : ℕ => Real.exp (-((n : ℝ) * a))) := by
    simpa using summable_pow_mul_exp_neg 0 ha
  have hcontinuous : ContinuousOn
      (fun y : ℝ => ∑' n : ℕ, mobiusDiscreteLaplaceTerm y n) (Ici a) := by
    refine continuousOn_tsum (fun n => ?_) hmajor (fun n y hy => ?_)
    · unfold mobiusDiscreteLaplaceTerm
      fun_prop
    · rw [mobiusDiscreteLaplaceTerm, norm_mul, Complex.norm_exp]
      have hmu : ‖((ArithmeticFunction.moebius n : ℤ) : ℂ)‖ ≤ 1 := by
        rw [Complex.norm_intCast]

`3-formalized/weil-polar-degeneracy-threshold-lean.md`: the pole-vanishing ground energy is

## Addendum 2026-09-03 — the pole-vanishing multiplier, and the status of the two RH links

**Multiplier (Lean, `RHTower.CCMRestrictedWeilPolarMultiplier`).** Two integrations by parts give
`∫ e^{sx} g'' = s² ∫ e^{sx} g` for every smooth compactly supported `g`
(`integral_exp_mul_deriv_deriv`), so `D = ∂² − 1/4`, whose Mellin symbol in the centred variable
is `s(s − 1)`, kills both pole coefficients: `D g` is a pole-vanishing strict-interior source for
every strict-interior source `g` (`isPolarConstrained_polarMultiplier`). Converse on paper: for a
pole-vanishing smooth `f`, `g := −e^{−|x|/2} ∗ f` is smooth, satisfies `D g = f`, and is compactly
supported because beyond the support of `f` it equals `−e^{∓x/2} ∫ e^{±y/2} f(y) dy = 0`. So the
pole-vanishing smooth core is exactly the image of `D`.

**Status of the RH links (deep inspection).** The corpus's `RH ⟸ positivity` chain runs through
zero-mean two-bump tests localizing Suzuki's screw form at `2Ψ(t)` and the pointwise criterion
`Ψ ≥ 0 ⇒ RH` (`riemannHypothesis_of_suzukiSmoothTestFormNonnegative`). Two-bump tests are not
pole-vanishing, and the localization of `Q(D g)` is at the fourth-order distribution `D²Ψ`, whose
sign is not controlled by `Ψ(t₀) < 0`; Cramer-correcting a negative two-bump test costs `O(1)`
coefficients and does not preserve negativity. The zero-side route (`xiOffRealSignTest`,
`XiGuinandWeilExplicitFormula`) lives on the resolvent test algebra, and the corpus records that
the explicit formula does not yet extend to general compactly supported tests (the full test
algebra gate, `weil-polarization-layer-state`). Hence `μ₀ > 0 at every aperture ⇒ RH` is a known
theorem (Bombieri 2000 / Yoshida 1992 on pole-vanishing tests, via `s(s−1)`-weighted Weil
positivity) but is not formalizable from the corpus's present assets without either extending the
explicit formula to compact tests or building a pole-vanishing analogue of the screw
localization. Both are formalization projects of a known theorem; neither is new knowledge.

**Prime-necessity observation (paper, not yet certified).** The exact archimedean form is
`∫ 2θ′(2πξ)|f̂(ξ)|² dξ` on pole-vanishing tests, and `θ′ < 0` on `|t| < 6.29`. A pole-vanishing
test of long support with Fourier mass concentrated near `|ξ| = 1/2` (for instance `D g` with `g`
a smooth window modulated at frequency `1/2`) therefore has negative archimedean form. So the
archimedean form alone is indefinite on the pole-vanishing subspace beyond an explicit aperture,
and the prime terms are necessary for Weil positivity there. Yoshida's numerics give archimedean
positivity up to support `(1/2, 2)`; the explicit indefiniteness threshold is a computable but
unrecorded number.

The result gives the exact positive classification of what all-order Euler ray algebra retains at

```text
complete bounded Euler ray modulo vanishing tails
```

In particular, an off-line residue character `tau_z` remains a finite-ray limit in the full

Therefore the missing RH compatibility cannot be obtained from:

# Attainment and the degeneracy threshold of the pole-vanishing Weil form — Lean certificate

- **ID:** `WEIL-ENTRY-001-L3`
- **Stage:** 3-formalized
- **Parent card:** `1-in-progress/weil-positivity-soft-prime-entry.md`
- **Module:** `GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower.CCMRestrictedWeilPolarGroundState` (imports the
  pole-vanishing ground energy module and `SuzukiSmallApertureGroundEnergy`; wired after
  `CCMRestrictedWeilPolarGroundEnergy`)
- **Axioms:** `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`; lint clean; no hypotheses.

## Statements

- `exists_polarConstrained_groundState`: at every aperture the pole-vanishing ground energy `μ₀`
  is attained by a normalized pole-vanishing form-domain vector. Proof: normalized near-minimizers
  have bounded form norm; the compact form embedding gives a physical limit of norm one; the limit
  is pole-vanishing by continuity of the pole coefficients; it lies in every closed sublevel set
  `{Q ≤ μ₀ + 1/(k+1)}`, and injectivity of the embedding identifies the sublevel witnesses across
  levels, so the witness has `Q ≤ μ₀`; the Rayleigh floor gives equality.
- `exists_small_aperture_polarGroundEnergy_pos`: `μ₀ > 0` below an explicit-existence aperture
  (from the corpus's small-aperture positivity of the full form, Suzuki 2026 Thm 1.4 side).
- `continuous_ccmRestrictedWeilPolarGroundEnergy`.
- `exists_polar_degeneracy_threshold`: if `μ₀(b) ≤ 0` for some `b`, there is `a*` with
  `μ₀(a*) = 0`, `μ₀ > 0` strictly below `a*`, and `μ₀ ≤ 0` strictly above `a*`.  The threshold
  is the infimum of the closed set `{μ₀ ≤ 0}` pulled back to the real line by a continuous
  extension constant below half the small-aperture radius.
- `polar_positivity_or_null_vector`: **the degeneracy law** — either `μ₀ > 0` at every aperture,
  or some aperture `a*` carries a normalized pole-vanishing vector `v*` with `Q(v*) = 0` while
  `Q ≥ 0` on the whole pole-vanishing subspace at `a*`.

## Reading

This is the pole-vanishing form of the Yoshida–Suzuki degeneracy corollary: the only way Weil
positivity on the pole-vanishing subspace can fail is through an attained null vector at a
threshold aperture, never discontinuously and never through a prime entering (the prime terms are
part of the exact form and `μ₀` is continuous through their thresholds). On paper the two RH links
are: RH ⇒ `μ₀ > 0` everywhere (Weil's form is a sum of `|f̂(ρ)|²`, and an entire function of
exponential type cannot vanish at all zeros by the zero-density comparison, Yoshida's Theorem 2),
and `μ₀ > 0` everywhere ⇒ RH (Weil's criterion on the pole-vanishing subspace, using the
multiplier `s(s−1)` to place any test packet in the subspace). Neither link is formalized here.

## Lean notes

- `show P at h` is not syntax; use `change P at h`.
- The threshold argument avoids the subtype topology by extending `μ₀` to the real line through
  `t ↦ ⟨max t (δ/2), _⟩` (`Continuous.subtype_mk`), which is continuous and constant below `δ/2`.
- `exists_nat_one_div_lt` and `le_of_forall_pos_le_add` pass the sublevel bounds to the limit.

# Projective spectrum of a graded ring

The projective spectrum of a graded commutative ring is the subtype of all homogeneous ideals that
are prime and do not contain the irrelevant ideal.
It is naturally endowed with a topology: the Zariski topology.

## Notation
- `A` is a commutative ring
- `σ` is a class of additive submonoids of `A`
- `𝒜 : ℕ → σ` is the grading of `A`;

## Main definitions

* `ProjectiveSpectrum 𝒜`: The projective spectrum of a graded ring `A`, or equivalently, the set of
  all homogeneous ideals of `A` that is both prime and relevant i.e. not containing irrelevant
  ideal. Henceforth, we call elements of projective spectrum *relevant homogeneous prime ideals*.
* `ProjectiveSpectrum.zeroLocus 𝒜 s`: The zero locus of a subset `s` of `A`
  is the subset of `ProjectiveSpectrum 𝒜` consisting of all relevant homogeneous prime ideals that
  contain `s`.
* `ProjectiveSpectrum.vanishingIdeal t`: The vanishing ideal of a subset `t` of
  `ProjectiveSpectrum 𝒜` is the intersection of points in `t` (viewed as relevant homogeneous prime
  ideals).
* `ProjectiveSpectrum.Top`: the topological space of `ProjectiveSpectrum 𝒜` endowed with the
  Zariski topology.
-/

@[expose] public section


noncomputable section

open DirectSum Pointwise SetLike TopCat TopologicalSpace CategoryTheory Opposite

variable {A σ : Type*}
variable [CommRing A] [SetLike σ A] [AddSubmonoidClass σ A]
variable (𝒜 : ℕ → σ) [GradedRing 𝒜]

/-- The projective spectrum of a graded commutative ring is the subtype of all homogeneous ideals
that are prime and do not contain the irrelevant ideal. -/
@[ext]
structure ProjectiveSpectrum where
  asHomogeneousIdeal : HomogeneousIdeal 𝒜
  isPrime : asHomogeneousIdeal.toIdeal.IsPrime
  not_irrelevant_le : ¬HomogeneousIdeal.irrelevant 𝒜 ≤ asHomogeneousIdeal

attribute [instance] ProjectiveSpectrum.isPrime

namespace ProjectiveSpectrum

instance (x : ProjectiveSpectrum 𝒜) : Ideal.IsPrime x.asHomogeneousIdeal.toIdeal := x.isPrime

/-- The zero locus of a set `s` of elements of a commutative ring `A` is the set of all relevant
homogeneous prime ideals of the ring that contain the set `s`.

An element `f` of `A` can be thought of as a dependent function on the projective spectrum of `𝒜`.
At a point `x` (a homogeneous prime ideal) the function (i.e., element) `f` takes values in the
quotient ring `A` modulo the prime ideal `x`. In this manner, `zeroLocus s` is exactly the subset
of `ProjectiveSpectrum 𝒜` where all "functions" in `s` vanish simultaneously. -/
def zeroLocus (s : Set A) : Set (ProjectiveSpectrum 𝒜) :=
  { x | s ⊆ x.asHomogeneousIdeal }

@[simp]
theorem mem_zeroLocus (x : ProjectiveSpectrum 𝒜) (s : Set A) :
    x ∈ zeroLocus 𝒜 s ↔ s ⊆ x.asHomogeneousIdeal :=

/-!
# Complex measure

This file defines a complex measure to be a vector measure with codomain `ℂ`.
Then we prove some elementary results about complex measures. In particular, we prove that
a complex measure is always in the form `s + it` where `s` and `t` are signed measures.

## Main definitions

* `MeasureTheory.ComplexMeasure.re`: obtains a signed measure `s` from a complex measure `c`
  such that `s i = (c i).re` for all measurable sets `i`.
* `MeasureTheory.ComplexMeasure.im`: obtains a signed measure `s` from a complex measure `c`
  such that `s i = (c i).im` for all measurable sets `i`.
* `MeasureTheory.SignedMeasure.toComplexMeasure`: given two signed measures `s` and `t`,
  `s.toComplexMeasure t` provides a complex measure of the form `s + it`.
* `MeasureTheory.ComplexMeasure.equivSignedMeasure`: is the equivalence between the complex
  measures and the type of the product of the signed measures with itself.

## Tags

Complex measure
-/

@[expose] public section


noncomputable section

open scoped MeasureTheory ENNReal NNReal

variable {α : Type*} {m : MeasurableSpace α}

namespace MeasureTheory

open VectorMeasure

/-- A `ComplexMeasure` is a `ℂ`-vector measure. -/
abbrev ComplexMeasure (α : Type*) [MeasurableSpace α] :=
  VectorMeasure α ℂ

namespace ComplexMeasure

/-- The real part of a complex measure is a signed measure. -/
@[simps! apply]
def re : ComplexMeasure α →ₗ[ℝ] SignedMeasure α :=
  mapRangeₗ Complex.reCLM Complex.continuous_re

/-- The imaginary part of a complex measure is a signed measure. -/
@[simps! apply]
def im : ComplexMeasure α →ₗ[ℝ] SignedMeasure α :=
  mapRangeₗ Complex.imCLM Complex.continuous_im

/-- Given `s` and `t` signed measures, `s + it` is a complex measure -/
@[simps!]
def _root_.MeasureTheory.SignedMeasure.toComplexMeasure (s t : SignedMeasure α) :
    ComplexMeasure α where
  measureOf' i := ⟨s i, t i⟩
  empty' := by rw [s.empty, t.empty]; rfl
  not_measurable' i hi := by rw [s.not_measurable hi, t.not_measurable hi]; rfl
  m_iUnion' _ hf hfdisj := (Complex.hasSum_iff _ _).2 ⟨s.m_iUnion hf hfdisj, t.m_iUnion hf hfdisj⟩

theorem _root_.MeasureTheory.SignedMeasure.toComplexMeasure_apply
    {s t : SignedMeasure α} {i : Set α} : s.toComplexMeasure t i = ⟨s i, t i⟩ := rfl

theorem toComplexMeasure_to_signedMeasure (c : ComplexMeasure α) :
    SignedMeasure.toComplexMeasure (ComplexMeasure.re c) (ComplexMeasure.im c) = c := rfl

theorem _root_.MeasureTheory.SignedMeasure.re_toComplexMeasure (s t : SignedMeasure α) :
    ComplexMeasure.re (SignedMeasure.toComplexMeasure s t) = s := rfl

theorem _root_.MeasureTheory.SignedMeasure.im_toComplexMeasure (s t : SignedMeasure α) :
    ComplexMeasure.im (SignedMeasure.toComplexMeasure s t) = t := rfl

/-- The complex measures form an equivalence to the type of pairs of signed measures. -/
@[simps]
def equivSignedMeasure : ComplexMeasure α ≃ SignedMeasure α × SignedMeasure α where
  toFun c := ⟨ComplexMeasure.re c, ComplexMeasure.im c⟩
  invFun := fun ⟨s, t⟩ => s.toComplexMeasure t
  left_inv c := c.toComplexMeasure_to_signedMeasure
  right_inv := fun ⟨s, t⟩ => Prod.ext (s.re_toComplexMeasure t) (s.im_toComplexMeasure t)

section

variable {R : Type*} [Semiring R] [Module R ℝ]
variable [ContinuousConstSMul R ℝ] [ContinuousConstSMul R ℂ]

/-- The complex measures form a linear isomorphism to the type of pairs of signed measures. -/
@[simps]
def equivSignedMeasureₗ : ComplexMeasure α ≃ₗ[R] SignedMeasure α × SignedMeasure α :=
  { equivSignedMeasure with
    map_add' := fun c d => by rfl
    map_smul' := by
      intro r c
      dsimp
      ext
      · simp [Complex.smul_re]
      · simp [Complex.smul_im] }

end

theorem absolutelyContinuous_ennreal_iff (c : ComplexMeasure α) (μ : VectorMeasure α ℝ≥0∞) :
    c ≪ᵥ μ ↔ ComplexMeasure.re c ≪ᵥ μ ∧ ComplexMeasure.im c ≪ᵥ μ := by
  constructor <;> intro h
  · constructor <;> · intro i hi; simp [h hi]
  · intro i hi
    rw [← Complex.re_add_im (c i), (_ : (c i).re = 0), (_ : (c i).im = 0)]
    exacts [by simp, h.2 hi, h.1 hi]

end ComplexMeasure

end MeasureTheory

/-!
# Lebesgue decomposition

This file proves the Lebesgue decomposition theorem for signed measures. The Lebesgue decomposition
theorem states that, given two σ-finite measures `μ` and `ν`, there exists a σ-finite measure `ξ`
and a measurable function `f` such that `μ = ξ + fν` and `ξ` is mutually singular with respect
to `ν`.

## Main definitions

* `MeasureTheory.SignedMeasure.HaveLebesgueDecomposition` : A signed measure `s` is said to have
  Lebesgue decomposition with respect to a measure `μ` if both the positive part and negative part
  of `s` have Lebesgue decomposition with respect to `μ`.
* `MeasureTheory.SignedMeasure.singularPart` : The singular part between a signed measure `s`
  and a measure `μ` is simply the singular part of the positive part of `s` with respect to `μ`
  minus the singular part of the negative part of `s` with respect to `μ`.
* `MeasureTheory.SignedMeasure.rnDeriv` : The Radon-Nikodym derivative of a signed
  measure `s` with respect to a measure `μ` is the Radon-Nikodym derivative of the positive part of
  `s` with respect to `μ` minus the Radon-Nikodym derivative of the negative part of `s` with
  respect to `μ`.

## Main results

* `MeasureTheory.SignedMeasure.singularPart_add_withDensity_rnDeriv_eq` :
  the Lebesgue decomposition theorem between a signed measure and a σ-finite positive measure.

## Tags

Lebesgue decomposition theorem
-/

@[expose] public section


noncomputable section

open scoped MeasureTheory NNReal ENNReal

open Set

variable {α : Type*} {m : MeasurableSpace α} {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure α}

namespace MeasureTheory

namespace SignedMeasure

open Measure

/-- A signed measure `s` is said to `HaveLebesgueDecomposition` with respect to a measure `μ`
if the positive part and the negative part of `s` both `HaveLebesgueDecomposition` with
respect to `μ`. -/
class HaveLebesgueDecomposition (s : SignedMeasure α) (μ : Measure α) : Prop where
  posPart : s.toJordanDecomposition.posPart.HaveLebesgueDecomposition μ
  negPart : s.toJordanDecomposition.negPart.HaveLebesgueDecomposition μ

attribute [instance] HaveLebesgueDecomposition.posPart

attribute [instance] HaveLebesgueDecomposition.negPart

theorem not_haveLebesgueDecomposition_iff (s : SignedMeasure α) (μ : Measure α) :
    ¬s.HaveLebesgueDecomposition μ ↔
      ¬s.toJordanDecomposition.posPart.HaveLebesgueDecomposition μ ∨
        ¬s.toJordanDecomposition.negPart.HaveLebesgueDecomposition μ :=
  ⟨fun h => not_or_of_imp fun hp hn => h ⟨hp, hn⟩, fun h hl => (not_and_or.2 h) ⟨hl.1, hl.2⟩⟩

-- `inferInstance` directly does not work
-- see Note [lower instance priority]
instance (priority := 100) haveLebesgueDecomposition_of_sigmaFinite (s : SignedMeasure α)
    (μ : Measure α) [SigmaFinite μ] : s.HaveLebesgueDecomposition μ where
  posPart := inferInstance
  negPart := inferInstance

instance haveLebesgueDecomposition_neg (s : SignedMeasure α) (μ : Measure α)
    [s.HaveLebesgueDecomposition μ] : (-s).HaveLebesgueDecomposition μ where
  posPart := by
    rw [toJordanDecomposition_neg, JordanDecomposition.neg_posPart]
    infer_instance
  negPart := by
    rw [toJordanDecomposition_neg, JordanDecomposition.neg_negPart]
    infer_instance

instance haveLebesgueDecomposition_smul (s : SignedMeasure α) (μ : Measure α)
    [s.HaveLebesgueDecomposition μ] (r : ℝ≥0) : (r • s).HaveLebesgueDecomposition μ where
  posPart := by
    rw [toJordanDecomposition_smul, JordanDecomposition.smul_posPart]
    infer_instance
  negPart := by
    rw [toJordanDecomposition_smul, JordanDecomposition.smul_negPart]
    infer_instance

instance haveLebesgueDecomposition_smul_real (s : SignedMeasure α) (μ : Measure α)
    [s.HaveLebesgueDecomposition μ] (r : ℝ) : (r • s).HaveLebesgueDecomposition μ := by
  by_cases! hr : 0 ≤ r
  · lift r to ℝ≥0 using hr
    exact s.haveLebesgueDecomposition_smul μ _
  · refine
      { posPart := by
          rw [toJordanDecomposition_smul_real, JordanDecomposition.real_smul_posPart_neg _ _ hr]
          infer_instance
        negPart := by
          rw [toJordanDecomposition_smul_real, JordanDecomposition.real_smul_negPart_neg _ _ hr]
          infer_instance }

/-- Given a signed measure `s` and a measure `μ`, `s.singularPart μ` is the signed measure
such that `s.singularPart μ + μ.withDensityᵥ (s.rnDeriv μ) = s` and
`s.singularPart μ` is mutually singular with respect to `μ`. -/
def singularPart (s : SignedMeasure α) (μ : Measure α) : SignedMeasure α :=
  (s.toJordanDecomposition.posPart.singularPart μ).toSignedMeasure -
    (s.toJordanDecomposition.negPart.singularPart μ).toSignedMeasure

# The fixed-shell coefficient law and its signed-permutation invariance

Pushing the unit-sphere measure forward along the coordinate map turns it into a law on the
coefficient space itself, so every statement about ensembles indexed by a coefficient vector
applies to the fixed-shell ensemble with no change of type.  Signed permutations are linear
isometries, so they preserve that law -- this is the fixed-shell replacement for the invariance of
the centred product Gaussian.

Main results:
* `shellCoefficientMap`, `shellCoefficientMeasure` — the coefficient law of the unit shell.
* `measurePreserving_signedPerm_shell` — **the shell law is invariant under signed permutations**.
* `isFiniteMeasure_shellCoefficientMeasure` — it is finite.

/-- The coordinate map from the unit sphere to the coefficient space. -/
def shellCoefficientMap (ι : Type*) [Fintype ι] :
    sphere (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ ι) 1 → (ι → ℝ) :=
  fun θ => WithLp.ofLp ((θ : EuclideanSpace ℝ ι))

theorem continuous_shellCoefficientMap :
    Continuous (shellCoefficientMap ι) :=
  (PiLp.continuous_ofLp 2 _).comp continuous_subtype_val

theorem measurable_shellCoefficientMap : Measurable (shellCoefficientMap ι) :=
  continuous_shellCoefficientMap.measurable

/-- **The fixed-shell coefficient law**: the unit-sphere measure read in coordinates. -/
def shellCoefficientMeasure (ι : Type*) [Fintype ι] : Measure (ι → ℝ) :=
  Measure.map (shellCoefficientMap ι) (volume : Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ ι)).toSphere

instance isFiniteMeasure_shellCoefficientMeasure :
    IsFiniteMeasure (shellCoefficientMeasure ι) := by
  constructor
  rw [shellCoefficientMeasure, Measure.map_apply measurable_shellCoefficientMap MeasurableSet.univ,
    Set.preimage_univ, Measure.toSphere_apply_univ]
  exact ENNReal.mul_lt_top (by simp) measure_ball_lt_top

theorem shellCoefficientMap_sphereMap {π : Equiv.Perm ι} {ε : ι → ℝ}
    (hε : ∀ i, ε i = 1 ∨ ε i = -1) (θ : sphere (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ ι) 1) :
    shellCoefficientMap ι (sphereMap (signedPermIsometry π hε) θ)
      = fun i => ε i * shellCoefficientMap ι θ (π i) := rfl

/-- **The fixed-shell coefficient law is invariant under every signed permutation.** -/
theorem measurePreserving_signedPerm_shell (π : Equiv.Perm ι) {ε : ι → ℝ}
    (hε : ∀ i, ε i = 1 ∨ ε i = -1) :
    MeasurePreserving (fun J : ι → ℝ => fun i => ε i * J (π i))
      (shellCoefficientMeasure ι) (shellCoefficientMeasure ι) := by
  set f : EuclideanSpace ℝ ι ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] EuclideanSpace ℝ ι := signedPermIsometry π hε with hf
  set T : (ι → ℝ) → (ι → ℝ) := fun J => fun i => ε i * J (π i) with hT
  have hTmeas : Measurable T := by
    refine measurable_pi_lambda _ fun i => ?_
    exact measurable_const.mul (measurable_pi_apply (π i))
  refine ⟨hTmeas, ?_⟩
  have hcomp : T ∘ shellCoefficientMap ι = shellCoefficientMap ι ∘ sphereMap f := by
    funext θ
    exact (shellCoefficientMap_sphereMap hε θ).symm
  calc Measure.map T (shellCoefficientMeasure ι)
      = Measure.map T (Measure.map (shellCoefficientMap ι)
          (volume : Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ ι)).toSphere) := rfl
    _ = Measure.map (T ∘ shellCoefficientMap ι)
          (volume : Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ ι)).toSphere :=
        Measure.map_map hTmeas measurable_shellCoefficientMap
    _ = Measure.map (shellCoefficientMap ι ∘ sphereMap f)
          (volume : Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ ι)).toSphere := by rw [hcomp]
    _ = Measure.map (shellCoefficientMap ι) (Measure.map (sphereMap f)
          (volume : Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ ι)).toSphere) :=
        (Measure.map_map measurable_shellCoefficientMap (measurable_sphereMap f)).symm
    _ = shellCoefficientMeasure ι := by
        rw [(measurePreserving_sphereMap f).map_eq]
        rfl

The positive-kernel classification leaves a sharp loophole: a signed nonlocal kernel can hide
finite collections of reflected Mellin rows through cancellation.  This module closes the whole
finite-measure class once the reflection implements every integer grade and its Jordan parts have
one common bilateral exponential window.

For positive delay `t`, write the signed Fermi-weighted output as `ν₊ - ν₋`, put `a=t⁻¹`, and put
`c=a F(t)`.  All-grade reflection says that `ν₊` and `ν₋ + c δ_a` have identical moments.
Local-exponential moment determinacy therefore gives the exact measure identity

`ν₊ = ν₋ + c δ_a`.

Undressing by reciprocal Fermi density `exp(x)+1` then fixes the net kernel mass as

`a (exp(a)+1)/(exp(t)+1)`,

the same singular local reflection weight found in the positive classification.  Total variation
dominates this net mass, so no polynomially tempered signed finite-measure implementation exists.

Thus signed cancellation does not rescue an analytically tempered nonlocal FZZ-P producer.  A
survivor must be genuinely distributional, lack every local exponential moment window, or retain
the forced essential singularity.

Moment determinacy is classical and imported from the corpus.  Candidate novelty is its exact
assembly with the Fermi source, Jordan cancellation, reciprocal undressing, and the FZZ-P route
consequence.

`[FZZ-P ROUTE KILL] [SIGNED NONLOCAL] [MOMENT DETERMINACY] [CANDIDATE NEW KNOWLEDGE]`

def fzzCigarParityUndressingDensity (x : ℝ) : ℝ := Real.exp x + 1

/-- Fermi-weighted reflected target: mass `t⁻¹ F(t)` at reciprocal delay. -/
def fzzCigarParitySignedTargetMeasure (t : FZZCigarPositiveDelay) : Measure ℝ :=
  ENNReal.ofReal ((t : ℝ)⁻¹ * fzzCigarPositiveDelayDensity t) •
    Measure.dirac ((t : ℝ)⁻¹)

private theorem fzzCigarPositiveDelayDensity_pos_signed
    (t : FZZCigarPositiveDelay) : 0 < fzzCigarPositiveDelayDensity t := by
  rw [fzzCigarPositiveDelayDensity, fzzCigarParityDelay_eq_fermi t.property]
  positivity

/-- Jordan data for an all-grade signed nonlocal reflection of the literal FZZ source.  The
exponential-window field is analytic tempering; reciprocal-Fermi integrability makes undressed
total variation finite. -/
structure FZZCigarParitySignedNonlocalFEReflectionData where
  positivePart : FZZCigarPositiveDelay → Measure ℝ
  negativePart : FZZCigarPositiveDelay → Measure ℝ
  positive_finite : ∀ t, IsFiniteMeasure (positivePart t)
  negative_finite : ∀ t, IsFiniteMeasure (negativePart t)
  undressing_positive_integrable : ∀ t,
    Integrable fzzCigarParityUndressingDensity (positivePart t)
  undressing_negative_integrable : ∀ t,
    Integrable fzzCigarParityUndressingDensity (negativePart t)
  common_window : ∀ t, ∃ b : ℝ, 0 < b ∧
    Set.Ioo (-b) b ⊆ integrableExpSet id (positivePart t) ∧
    Set.Ioo (-b) b ⊆ integrableExpSet id
      (negativePart t + fzzCigarParitySignedTargetMeasure t)
  all_grades : ∀ t n,
    ∫ x : ℝ, x ^ n ∂positivePart t =
      ∫ x : ℝ, x ^ n ∂(negativePart t + fzzCigarParitySignedTargetMeasure t)

/-- **All-grade signed collapse.**  One common exponential window turns equality of every
integer Mellin row into equality of the complete Fermi-weighted measures. -/
theorem FZZCigarParitySignedNonlocalFEReflectionData.fermiWeightedMeasure_eq
    (D : FZZCigarParitySignedNonlocalFEReflectionData)
    (t : FZZCigarPositiveDelay) :
    D.positivePart t = D.negativePart t + fzzCigarParitySignedTargetMeasure t := by
  letI : IsFiniteMeasure (D.positivePart t) := D.positive_finite t
  letI : IsFiniteMeasure (D.negativePart t) := D.negative_finite t
  letI : IsFiniteMeasure
      (D.negativePart t + fzzCigarParitySignedTargetMeasure t) := by
    refine IsFiniteMeasure.mk ?_
    simp [fzzCigarParitySignedTargetMeasure,
      measure_lt_top (D.negativePart t) Set.univ]
  obtain ⟨b, hb, hpos, hneg⟩ := D.common_window t
  exact HTGeometry.measure_eq_of_forall_real_moment_eq hb hpos hneg (D.all_grades t)

private theorem integrable_fzzCigarParityUndressingDensity_signedTarget
    (t : FZZCigarPositiveDelay) :
    Integrable fzzCigarParityUndressingDensity
      (fzzCigarParitySignedTargetMeasure t) := by
  have hcpos : 0 < (t : ℝ)⁻¹ * fzzCigarPositiveDelayDensity t :=
    mul_pos (inv_pos.mpr t.property) (fzzCigarPositiveDelayDensity_pos_signed t)
  rw [fzzCigarParitySignedTargetMeasure]
  apply (integrable_smul_measure (ENNReal.ofReal_pos.mpr hcpos).ne' (by simp)).mpr
  apply integrable_dirac
  simp [fzzCigarParityUndressingDensity]
